title: Fully silicided nickel wordlines replace tungsten fill
idea: Imposed scarcity: no W and no WF6. Fill the wordline trench with doped amorphous silicon, cap it with Ni(Pt) and anneal so the whole trench converts to NiSi (full silicidation); the work function is tuned by dopant pile-up at the gate interface.
why: Removes tungsten and fluorine from the cell; work-function engineering by dopant segregation can cut GIDL and so the leakage tail that forces refresh; NiSi at ~15 uOhm-cm competes with narrow W lines.

title: Fab waste heat drives ceramic membrane distillation for zero discharge
idea: Separating pure water from brine has a thermodynamic minimum near 1 kWh/m3 while a fab rejects ~100 MW of 30-45 C process-cooling heat; use that temperature difference to drive vacuum membrane distillation of RO reject and CMP effluent through silane-hydrophobized alumina/SiC membranes instead of PTFE/PVDF.
why: Raises water recovery from ~60-70% to >95% on free heat, cutting withdrawal ~30-50% at drought-prone US sites with PFAS-free membranes.

title: Anodic alumina nanopore templates host ultra-high-aspect capacitor arrays
idea: Box [MIM cap in anodic alumina pores | Si access below | voltage SA | capacitor layer over storage contacts | e-beam-evaporated Al film (vacuum, no gas) | two-step oxalic-acid anodization guided by NIL dimples]: anodize a 3 um Al film into self-ordered 25-40 nm pores registered to imprinted dimples, wet-open the barrier oxide, and deposit TiN/dielectric/TiN inside.
why: Capacitor charge wall and etch intensity: AR 100-200 holes cost about as much as a plating bath, with no fluorocarbon etch and no rare gases; Al is abundant and US-made.

title: Electrophoretic BaTiO3 nanocube monolayers form high-k capacitors cold
idea: Effect: electrophoresis plus size-dependent permittivity. 15 nm BaTiO3 nanocubes, already crystallized by hydrothermal synthesis at ~200 C, drift under DC bias into trenches or pores and pack face to face. An ALD AlOx infill at 250 C seals pinholes, giving k ~100-300 with no 700 C perovskite anneal.
why: Hf/Zr-free route to the k~70 the capacitor wall needs (fact 1); Ba and Ti are widely sourced; nothing exceeds 250 C.

title: Size-effect-optimized NiAl intermetallic wordlines replace buried tungsten
idea: Effect: Fuchs-Sondheimer surface and Mayadas-Shatzkes grain-boundary scattering penalize long-mean-free-path metals below 20 nm. B2-ordered NiAl and CuAl2 have ~5 nm electron mean free paths and need no TiN barrier, so at 10-15 nm widths they match or beat W+TiN. Co-sputter or ALD the layers, then order them with a short anneal.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry; reclaiming barrier volume gives 20-40% lower wordline RC, and Ni and Al are widely sourced.

title: Substitute domestic glass-core substrates for single-source ABF build-up film
idea: Build DRAM and HBM package substrates on borosilicate glass cores with laser-drilled through-glass vias and US-made photo-imageable polyimide redistribution layers instead of Ajinomoto ABF laminates.
why: Removes a near-monopoly packaging material; glass flatness permits finer bump pitch and lower warpage, raising stacked-package yield.

title: Mature-node SiON periphery wafers bonded under the array
idea: Worsen: build the 49% of the die that is periphery in the same leading-edge flow, with Hf/La high-k metal gates and EUV. Flip: make the periphery logic on 28-40 nm SiON-gate wafers in existing U.S. mature fabs and hybrid-bond it beneath an array-only wafer, so hafnium, lanthanum and EUV appear only where the cell needs them.
why: Hf/La and EUV intensity, periphery area and U.S. manufacturability: the array die shrinks ~40%.

title: Combinatorial abundant-element dielectric library for capacitors
idea: Within $1M/24 months: co-sputter graded Ti-Al-Si-Mg-Ca-O-N thin-film libraries (crustal-abundant elements only) on probe-array wafers, auto-measure k, leakage and breakdown across ~10,000 compositions, and hand the top 10 to ALD recipe development.
why: Searches for a k>=60, low-leakage capacitor dielectric with no Hf, Zr, Sr or rare earths, aimed straight at the capacitor charge wall, at lab cost.

title: Acidithiobacillus bioleaching loop for scrapped DIMMs and fab sludge
idea: Run a bioreactor chain: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans leaches Cu and Ni from shredded modules, cyanogenic Chromobacterium then recovers gold, and engineered tungstate-binding TupA proteins capture W and Mo from CMP and etch sludge.
why: Turns millions of retired DIMMs and fab waste into domestic W, Au, Cu and Ta at ambient temperature and low energy, easing the tungsten (China ~80%) chokepoint.

title: Deuterium-annealed access transistors slow hot-carrier aging at 125 C
idea: Magnify the isotope mass: passivate Si/SiO2 interface traps with deuterium instead of hydrogen in the final anneal, using D2 from domestic heavy-water electrolysis; the heavier bond resists hot-carrier and BTI desorption 10-50x better.
why: Lets thinner, smaller-margin access devices meet a 10-year 125 C lifetime instead of over-sizing cells, at tiny extra cost.

title: Deuterium-annealed access transistors shrink the leakage tail
idea: Worsen: let hydrogen-passivated interface traps depassivate under stress, so retention tails grow and refresh rates climb. Flip: do the final forming-gas anneal with deuterium. The heavier Si-D bond resists hot-carrier and GIDL-driven breaking, which tightens the access-transistor leakage tail that sets refresh.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit): deuterium comes from abundant heavy water, and a 2x tighter tail would halve the refresh rate.

title: Interference lithography with neon-free solid-state lasers for array lines
idea: Revive 1970s holographic-grating interference lithography for the periodic DRAM array: two or four beams from a 213 nm fifth-harmonic solid-state laser print dense line/space and hole arrays without masks, with DUV steppers used only for trims and periphery.
why: No EUV, no array masks and no neon (ArF/KrF excimer lasers need neon, concentrated in Ukraine); claims 60 nm-pitch arrays for ~10% of an EUV scanner's capital.

title: Silicon-carbide furnace ware removes the second quartz dependency
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero HPQ anywhere in the fab, not just in crucibles. Replace quartz diffusion tubes, boats, injectors and bell jars with CVD-SiC-coated or recrystallized SiC, plus single-crystal silicon parts machined from ingot tops and tails.
why: Fab quartzware also depends on Spruce Pine-grade sand; SiC parts last ~3-5x longer at high temperature and survive HF cleans, cutting consumable volume and chokepoint exposure.

title: Osteoclast sealed-zone catalytic etching of capacitor holes
idea: Osteoclasts dissolve bone by sealing a tiny compartment and pumping acid into it. Form storage-node holes by metal-assisted chemical etching: a patterned Ag or Cu catalyst dot burrows straight down through a sacrificial silicon or SiGe mold in dilute HF/H2O2 on a wet bench, then the mold is oxidized or replaced, so no long C4F6/C4F8 plasma etch is needed.
why: The HAR capacitor etch is the biggest fluorocarbon-gas and etch-tool-time sink; catalytic etching reaches 100:1+ on cheap wet benches, cutting high-GWP perfluorocarbons and etch capital.

title: Recovered Memory Credit counts reused bits toward CHIPS targets
idea: Worsen: give subsidies only for new fab wafers, so a reused bit earns nothing. Flip: create a U.S. Recovered Memory Credit in CHIPS and federal procurement, where certified reused or repaired GB count toward supply targets, backed by extended producer responsibility take-back for servers.
why: U.S. memory supply and scarce-resource intensity: unlocks domestic refurbishment capacity years before any new fab.

title: Po helium is a fab export: closed-loop recapture at every tool
idea: Po: 'the fab exports helium instead of importing it.' Extracted: hood every helium user (ESC backside cooling exhaust, leak checkers, load-lock purge, carrier gas) with point-of-use recovery manifolds feeding a central compressor, a polymer-membrane pre-concentrator and a cryogenic purifier back to 6N, so purchases shrink to make-up for leakage.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% of supply offline since March 2026): 85-95% recovery cuts purchased helium ~10x and makes the fab immune to spot shortages; payback likely under 2 years at 2026 prices.

title: Camel-nose countercurrent water recovery from fab exhaust
idea: Camels recover water from exhaled breath with cooled, hygroscopic nasal turbinates. Put cyclically cooled, desiccant-coated turbinate heat exchangers in wet-scrubber and cooling-tower exhausts that capture vapour on the way out and release it as condensate during reverse-flow regeneration, feeding the UPW reclaim plant.
why: A DRAM megafab uses tens of ML of water a day and loses much of it as vapour; recovering 20-30% of evaporative loss eases siting in dry US states such as Idaho and Arizona.

title: Rooftop solar: recycled PV silicon cast into dummy and monitor wafers
idea: Stimulus 'rooftop solar panel' -> a 10-person shop recovers silicon from end-of-life PV modules, recasts it by directional solidification and cores/slices 300 mm rounds for dummy, monitor and temporary-carrier wafers that need no prime Cz silicon.
why: Test and dummy wafers are often ~15-30% of fab wafer starts; moving them off prime Cz cuts crucibles, polysilicon and crystal-growth energy.

title: Hummingbird torpor mode for fab tool gas purges
idea: Hummingbirds drop their metabolism ~95% at night. Give every etch, CVD and implant tool a predictive torpor state, keyed to the MES dispatch queue, that cuts helium backside and carrier purges to a trickle seal flow when no wafer is due for N minutes and restores full flow seconds before the next lot arrives.
why: Tools idle 20-40% of the time, often with purges still flowing; could cut fab helium and specialty-gas use 15-30% with software and valves alone while Qatar is offline.

title: Thermally drawn preform ribbons shrink centimeter laminates into nanoscale cells
idea: Ideal: draw memory like optical fiber, kilometers at a time. Closest: stack a cm-scale preform of glass, oxide semiconductor and low-melting metal (Sn-Zn or Al alloy) laminates in a cell cross-section, thermally draw it 1000-10,000x into ribbons whose layers shrink to 10-50 nm, then cut and tile ribbons orthogonally into crossbar or gain-cell tiers.
why: 100x: draw towers produce km/hour at ~$0.01/m and define features by geometric draw-down, not lithography; a speculative >=100x $/GB path from abundant glass, oxide and metal. Trades interlayer diffusion during draw, coarse tiling contacts and unproven semiconductor quality.

title: Substitute additive printed circuits for etched-and-plated memory module boards
idea: Print DIMM and CXL board traces with copper nanoparticle ink by aerosol jet or laser-induced forward transfer, sinter photonically, and print vias instead of drilling, plating and etching.
why: Subtractive PCB fabrication uses large plating and etch-rinse volumes per square meter of board; additive printing cuts module-board water >10x and eliminates copper etchant waste.

title: Flowable oxide fills and self-planarizes, ending ceria STI polish
idea: Combine trench fill and planarization (zero masks): flowable-CVD silazane oxide fills STI and levels like a liquid, then a timed dry etch-back endpointed on the pad nitride replaces the ceria CMP and post-CMP clean.
why: Removes rare-earth ceria slurry and hundreds of liters of UPW per wafer for CMP/cleans; flowable fill also voids less in 10 nm array trenches.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from a fluorine-free precursor
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 (no WF6) directly in the buried-wordline trench. Without fluorine there is nothing to attack the gate oxide, so the 2-3 nm TiN barrier that W needs can be removed, and at 10-15 nm widths Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistance than TiN/W.
why: Takes China-dominated tungsten (~80%) and WF6 out of the cell array, for ~20-30% lower wordline RC or a ~2 nm narrower trench at the same RC.

title: Catastrophe bonds finance second sources for single-point chokepoints
idea: Insurers use parametric cat bonds that pay out on a measurable trigger. DRAM makers and hyperscalers pool premiums into a 'chokepoint bond' that pays automatically if Spruce Pine output, Qatari helium shipments or WF6 import prices cross thresholds, while the standing premium pool funds qualification of alternates (Norwegian quartz, synthetic crucibles, U.S. helium).
why: Prices tail risk so second sources that look uneconomic in calm years get funded; cuts expected lost DRAM output from single-region chokepoints.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride crucible supplies the wafer's nitrogen doping
idea: Combine crucible and dopant source (zero masks): a dense, non-wetting Si3N4 crucible is reused across 10-50 melts, and its slow dissolution supplies the 1e14-1e15 cm-3 nitrogen DRAM wafers already need for void control, with oxygen added by gas.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine quartz crucible consumable entirely and a separate nitrogen-doping step; risk is nitride precipitate inclusions.

title: Solid-state 193 nm lasers eliminate neon and fluorine gas
idea: Worsen: make every immersion DUV scanner burn neon sourced from a war zone, plus fluorine-rich gas fills. Flip: replace ArF excimer lasers with fiber-laser-pumped solid-state sources that reach 193 nm by cascaded harmonic generation in CLBO-type borate crystals grown domestically, so no rare gas is needed.
why: Neon chokepoint (historically ~50% from Ukraine) and fluorine handling: DRAM uses ~15-25 ArF layers, so the gas dependency goes away entirely.

title: Pre-plasma wet etching returns for non-critical DRAM layers
idea: Revive 1970s wet chemical etching (hot phosphoric acid for nitride, buffered HF for oxide, aqueous metal etches with recycled etchant) for coarse layers, replacing fluorocarbon plasma steps that also need helium backside wafer cooling.
why: Cuts PFAS/fluorinated greenhouse-gas use and helium consumption, with no EUV; claims 20-30% fewer plasma steps per wafer.

title: Gray-tone mask and dual-tone resist merge two EUV layers
idea: Combine two critical layers in one EUV exposure: a gray-tone mask (partial-transmission absorber) gives two dose levels that a dual-tone resist resolves into two solubility states, developed sequentially (positive, then negative) into two stacked hardmasks; this removes a mask rather than adding one.
why: Cuts one of 5-7 EUV layers (~15-20% of per-wafer EUV time freed), easing the single-supplier chokepoint and ~1 MW/tool energy.

title: Overflow fusion-draw glass panels host U.S.-made panel DRAM
idea: Display glass is made by overflow fusion draw in Kentucky; on those 3 m panels, use U.S.-built i-line steppers and PECVD to stack 8-16 tiers of indium-free oxide gain-cell DRAM at ~1 um features, getting density from stacking and panel area instead of shrinking.
why: Needs no silicon wafers, no CZ crucibles, no EUV and no foreign litho; at ~1 um and 16 tiers a panel holds ~100 GB/m^2 at display-backplane cost (~$5/GB), a slow bulk-DRAM tier for CXL.

title: Fast-track qualification protocol for abundant-element material swaps
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: a consortium pre-builds shared JEDEC test vehicles, accelerated-stress datasets and failure-physics models for each abundant-element substitute (TiSi2 for W, Mg-Zn-Si-O for IGZO, spinel for yttria). A fab can then qualify a swap with a ~6-month delta test instead of a 2-3 year full requalification.
why: Qualification time, not chemistry, is the real barrier to dropping Hf, W, Co, Ru, Ta, In and Ga. Cutting it ~4x de-risks supply shocks and favors U.S. Earth-abundant supply chains.

title: Substitute area-selective deposition for resist-pattern-etch-strip loops
idea: Grow films only where wanted by first patterning inhibitor monolayers (UV-cleaved aminosilane SAMs or DUV-written carbon), then running ALD that nucleates only on uninhibited regions, deleting resist coat, develop, etch, strip and their cleans.
why: Each lithography loop carries ~5-8 wet steps; ASD-built layers cut water per patterned layer >10x and save ArF/EUV exposures.

title: Borax geologist builds FeRAM from boron-aluminum nitride
idea: Persona: a geologist at the borax pit in Boron, California. Use wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N (x ~0.07-0.15), sputtered below 400 C, as the ferroelectric in 1T1C FeRAM. Its square hysteresis, with Pr above 100 uC/cm2, switches far more charge per area than a DRAM dielectric.
why: Non-volatile, with ~10x the charge density, which shrinks capacitor aspect ratio sharply. No Hf, Zr or Sc, and boron and aluminum are abundant in the U.S. Risk: the ~5 MV/cm coercive field needs fatigue engineering.

title: Wartime materials board: per-gigabyte chokepoint-intensity procurement standard
idea: WWII production boards rationed tin and rubber by making designers report and cap use per unit. Require a certified 'chokepoint ledger' per gigabyte (mg W, liters He, g HPQ, g PFAS, liters UPW) for CHIPS-funded and DoD purchases, with price preferences for parts under a declining cap, like CAFE standards for memory.
why: Creates market pull for every substitution idea; targets a 50% cut in chokepoint intensity per GB in 5 years.

title: Cobalt-free Fe-B/MgO tunnel junctions crystallized under 350 C
idea: Effect: interfacial perpendicular anisotropy from Fe 3d-O 2p hybridization at the Fe/MgO interface. Drop Co entirely and use Mg or Al boron-sink caps instead of Ta/W, so Fe-B free and reference layers crystallize from the MgO template at <=350 C while keeping TMR >150%.
why: Cobalt (DRC ~70%), Ta and W removed from MRAM working-memory stacks; anneal stays inside the 400 C budget.

title: Supercritical-CO2 cleaning replaces most ultrapure-water wet cleans
idea: Ideal: a fab with no water. Closest: replace post-etch residue removal, post-CMP clean and capacitor-hole cleans with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent/chelator doses, which penetrates 100:1 holes with zero surface tension and is >95% recycled by depressurize-recompress loops.
why: DRAM fabs use ~10-20 M gal/day UPW; moving ~40% of cleans to scCO2 cuts water/wastewater proportionally and removes capillary collapse of tall capacitors (yield gain).

title: Substitute continuous vacuum for air between front-end process steps
idea: Link deposition, etch, anneal and inspection into long vacuum-transfer cluster lines where a wafer stays under vacuum for ~30 consecutive steps, so native oxide never grows and airborne particles never land, deleting the pre-clean before most steps.
why: Pre-cleans are the most frequent wet steps; a vacuum-continuum front end removes most of them for >10x less UPW in those modules, and cleaner interfaces shrink the leakage tail.

title: Strain-switched iron-aluminum nanomagnets on AlN, magnetoelectric memory
idea: Effect: inverse magnetostriction. A voltage across a sputtered AlN piezo layer strains an Fe-Al (Alfenol) nanomagnet and rotates its easy axis to toggle the bit for ~1 fJ, read through MgO tunnel magnetoresistance. Avoids Ga (Galfenol), Sc (ScAlN), Co, and the Pt/Ir/Ru of SOT and pinning stacks.
why: Energy per bit (voltage floor, fact 10) and scarce-element intensity: ~100x lower write energy than STT-MRAM, using abundant Fe, Al and N.

title: Thin-film magnetic memory on glass, read by cobalt-free permalloy spin valves
idea: 1960s thin-film magnetic memories deposited permalloy dots on glass but died on tiny inductive read signals and bulky drivers. Keep the glass and the permalloy, but read each dot with a NiFe/Cu/NiFe pseudo-spin-valve (thick and thin NiFe layers of different coercivity, ~5% GMR) and write with on-glass stripline current selected by oxide TFTs.
why: Removes Co, Pt, Ir, Ru, Ta and MgO from magnetic memory stacks; Ni, Fe, Cu are diversified; nonvolatile with unlimited endurance, so no refresh; cheap m2 glass substrate.

title: Po light digs the holes: electrochemical macroporous silicon trench capacitors
idea: Po: 'let light dig the holes.' Extracted: seed pits with a KrF stepper, then anodize n-type silicon in HF under backside illumination so pores grow straight to aspect ratios of 100-250 with no plasma; line them with thermal oxide/nitride and fill with doped poly to form trench storage capacitors.
why: Capacitor charge wall (AR ~115 needed) reached without plasma etch or high-k: at ~0.4 um pore pitch and AR ~200, Cs of 30-60 fF with ONO, which relaxes refresh; no Hf, Zr, W or fluorocarbon gas.

title: Maskless interference lithography prints DRAM array lattices without EUV
idea: A cell array is a perfect 2D lattice whose information content is a few numbers, not a mask; three-beam 193 nm immersion interference writes the hexagonal hole lattice using ~100% of the photons, spacer pitch division shrinks it, and a relaxed DUV cut mask defines array edges.
why: Replaces 2-4 EUV array layers (single supplier, ~1 MW per scanner) with low-cost interference optics; array litho capex down ~5x.

title: Sugar-based block copolymers self-assemble 4.5-nanometer DRAM grids without EUV
idea: Self-assembly pitch is set by the Flory-Huggins parameter (chi*N >= 10.5); carbohydrate-polystyrene block copolymers have chi ~10x that of PS-b-PMMA, reaching ~9 nm pitch. Pattern a 4F2 vertical oxide-channel gain-cell array at F~4.5 nm (81 nm2/cell) with DUV chemical prepatterns guiding the assembly.
why: 81 vs 864 nm2 = ~10.7x density; replaces 5-7 EUV layers (single supplier, MW-class tools) with spin-coat and anneal using a bio-derived polymer. Defectivity is the risk.

title: Fluoropolymer-free chemical and ultrapure-water wetted paths
idea: Wetted parts need only two properties, ppt-level metal extractables and chemical inertness; map each fluid to the cheapest material meeting both: PE/UHMWPE for UPW and HF, fused-silica- or sapphire-lined steel for hot sulfuric/peroxide, UPE filter membranes instead of PTFE, and CVD-SiC-coated valve seats.
why: Removes PFA/PTFE/PVDF (PFAS) from fab plumbing ahead of PFAS bans and fluoropolymer supplier exits, with equal or lower extractables.

title: Substitute dry coolers and CO2 heat pumps for evaporative towers
idea: Reject fab heat through dry air coolers, and use transcritical CO2 heat pumps to lift low-grade process-cooling heat to 70-90 C for UPW preheat, HVAC reheat and district heating instead of evaporating it in cooling towers.
why: Cooling towers are ~25-35% of fab consumptive water; removing evaporation cuts that share >10x while reusing ~20-30% of rejected heat.

title: Desolder, retest, rebin: die-level DRAM harvesting from e-waste
idea: Scale jump from discarded device to die: reflow DRAM packages off retired phones, laptops, GPU boards and DIMMs, then screen them on existing ATE testers at trailing test houses for speed and retention. Re-ball the good parts onto new modules for edge, IoT and capacity tiers.
why: Billions of retired devices hold working DRAM, and 10% recovery could add several percent of annual bit supply with no new wafers.

title: ALD hermetic wafer-level seal replaces epoxy mold compound
idea: Minify the package to a 1 um skin: seal finished memory dies at wafer level with ALD Al2O3/SiN multilayers and a metal seal ring, eliminating epoxy mold compound with its antimony and halogen flame retardants and fused-quartz filler.
why: The inorganic, moisture-proof seal survives 125 C for 10 years and 85/85 humidity testing; removes antimony (China-dominated) and HPQ-derived filler; package volume ~10x smaller.

title: Dirty bulk, clean skin: metallurgical silicon substrate under thick epi
idea: Inverts 'the whole wafer must be 11N electronic grade': use upgraded-metallurgical-grade (5-6N) seed-cast mono silicon as the substrate, add a buried phosphorus/aluminum gettering layer and a carbon-doped epitaxial diffusion barrier, then grow a 10 um high-purity epitaxial skin from silane where all devices live.
why: UMG silicon needs ~15-20 kWh/kg vs ~50-70 kWh/kg for Siemens polysilicon (~3x lower embodied energy per wafer) and can come from US/Norway metallurgical plants instead of concentrated polysilicon makers.

title: Substitute end-of-life solar panels for virgin polysilicon feedstock
idea: Thermally delaminate retired solar panels, chemically strip silver, aluminum and AR coatings, then hydrochlorinate the recovered silicon to trichlorosilane and redeposit it as 11N polysilicon for DRAM ingots.
why: Tens of Mt of panels retire by 2050; recovered silicon skips carbothermic quartz reduction (~11 kWh/kg) and imported poly, creating a domestic, low-energy feedstock loop.

title: Zero-liquid-discharge water loop using fab waste-heat membrane distillation
idea: Box [water source: RO reject + CMP/wet-bench rinse | heat source: 30-60 C process-cooling return | unit: membrane distillation + crystallizer | output: UPW feed]: recover >95% of reject water using heat the fab already throws away and crystallize the salts.
why: Water intensity: cuts net fab water withdrawal >80%, which makes DRAM fabs siteable in arid US states (AZ, TX, NM).

title: Smelter-friendly element palette for DRAM back end
idea: Worsen: scatter W, Ru, Co, Ta, Hf, La and Au across every chip so no recycler can recover anything. Flip: adopt design rules that limit the die and package to a minimal palette (Si, O, N, Al, Ti, Cu plus one capacitor metal) chosen to fit copper-smelter flowsheets, so e-scrap DRAM becomes a net-positive feed.
why: Scarce-resource intensity and recyclability: cuts the critical-element count per die from ~15 to ~6.

title: Supercritical CO2 and ozone dry cleaning replaces most UPW rinses
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | single-wafer scCO2 + co-solvent + dissolved O3 cleaner with CO2 recompression loop]: strip post-etch residue and particles inside high-AR capacitor holes with supercritical CO2, which has no surface tension and so causes no pattern collapse, recovering >95% of the CO2.
why: Water and pattern collapse at AR 70+: could cut wet-clean UPW ~50-70%, eliminate IPA drying and allow taller capacitors without stiction.

title: Pencil lead: intercalated graphite buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'pencil lead' -> graphite is the ultimate abundant conductor once doped. Fill the buried-wordline trench with CVD nanographite grown from CH4 on a thin Ni/Cu catalyst, then intercalate FeCl3 or Br2 so in-plane resistivity approaches ~5-10 uOhm-cm with basal planes aligned along the line.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry from DRAM's highest-volume metal; carbon from natural gas is effectively unlimited.

title: Anodized-aluminum nanopores as lithography-free capacitor molds on aluminum sheet
idea: Anodic-alumina nanopore MIM capacitors reached very high capacitance in university labs but never shipped because pore-ordering defects made single pores unreliable. Use the aluminum sheet as substrate: anodize self-ordered 30-60 nm pores 1-2 um deep, line with ALD TiN/Al2O3/TiN, and define each cell as a bundle of ~50-100 pores so defects average out, with oxide TFTs on the planarized alumina above.
why: 30-60:1 capacitor holes with no lithography, no EUV and no fluorocarbon plasma (oxalic-acid anodization at room temperature); ~100 fF/um2; aluminum is abundant and smelted in North America.

title: Tin-oxide seed grows hafnium-free rutile titania with k near 100
idea: Magnify k ~2.5x: a 2 nm SnO2 seed (rutile lattice) on the bottom electrode makes ALD TiO2 crystallize as high-k rutile below 450 C, with Al doping to tame leakage. It replaces ZrO2/HfO2 and the Ru-oxide templates used before.
why: Same Cs at aspect ratio ~30 instead of 70 (fact 1), removing hafnium and zirconium and halving the hardest etch; Sn and Ti are abundant.

title: Periphery on reclaimed wafers with old-node, hafnium-free gates
idea: Rearrange array and periphery onto separate wafers: build the 49% periphery on reclaimed monitor wafers at an older node with poly/SiON gates (no Hf, no EUV), then hybrid-bond it under the cell array.
why: Removes hafnium HKMG and EUV from half the die area and moves half the silicon onto recycled wafers; aims at ~30% less prime silicon and Hf per bit.

title: Nacre-stacked titania nanosheets printed as hafnium-free capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre's brick-and-mortar layering: exfoliate layered titanate into 1 nm Ti0.87O2 nanosheets (k~125) and lay them down roll-to-roll by Langmuir-Blodgett transfer, interleaved with sub-nm polymer mortar that blocks leakage paths at sheet edges. Use the film as the storage capacitor of printed oxide-TFT memory cells or as decoupling sheets on DRAM modules.
why: Titanium is abundant and US-sourced; k ~100+ at ~10 nm without Hf/Zr or vacuum ALD lets printed cells hold ~fF in um2 footprints.

title: Hafnium-free periphery: array bonded onto mature SiON-poly CMOS wafer
idea: Box [standard 1T1C array | Si access | sense amps on bottom wafer | Cu-Cu hybrid-bonded CMOS-bonded-array | array wafer + 28-40 nm SiON/poly periphery wafer | split fab]: build sense amps and decoders on a mature node with no HfO2/La high-k metal gate and no EUV, then bond the array wafer on top.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die and DRAM's only HKMG/Hf user: moves half the die to depreciated, EUV-free tools and removes Hf/La from DRAM while shrinking the array die ~40%.

title: Hafnium-free periphery on mature SiON wafers bonded under array
idea: Imposed scarcity: no hafnium and no EUV in the periphery. Build sense amps, decoders and I/O on a separate 40 nm poly/SiON CMOS wafer in any mature U.S. fab and hybrid-bond it face-to-face under the array wafer.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die; moving it to a Hf-free, EUV-free, depreciated node cuts EUV layers and scarce precursors per bit and frees array area for ~1.5-1.8x bits per array wafer.

title: ACSR power-line composite conductors replace tungsten array lines
idea: Overhead power lines pair conductive aluminum with a strong steel core. Adapt this for a capacitor-free BEOL array: wordlines and bitlines are Al cores with a 1-2 nm Mo or TiN skin that blocks electromigration and diffusion, which works because capacitor-free BEOL cells never exceed ~400 C.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and the tantalum barrier from array lines. Aluminum is abundant and smelted in the US, and low-temperature capacitor-free flows make it viable again.

title: Aluminum boron nitride capacitor: linear daily, ferroelectric at shutdown
idea: Minify hafnium and zirconium to zero: use wurtzite AlBN (abundant Al, B, N) as the capacitor dielectric. In normal use it runs below its coercive field as an ordinary linear DRAM capacitor, and it is switched as a ferroelectric only at power-down to save the memory image.
why: Its ferroelectric Curie point is far above 125 C, so saved polarization holds for 10 years, and daily operation never switches the film, so endurance is effectively unlimited; Hf-free.

title: Partial-good HBM stacks resold as shorter-height stacks
idea: Scale shift from die to stack: instead of scrapping 12-high HBM stacks with one or two failed core dies, fuse off those dies through base-die stack-ID remapping. The stacks ship as 8- or 10-high capacity parts for inference cards.
why: Recovers much of the 20-30% HBM yield loss as usable bits, with no extra wafer starts.

title: Organic-food certification model for PFAS-free capacitor-free memory
idea: Copy USDA Organic's audited-label model. Certify memory made in flows free of perfluorinated etch gases, PFAS photoacid generators and fluoropolymer wetted parts, which becomes achievable because a capacitor-free cell drops the 60:1 fluorocarbon etch, and sell it at a premium to EU buyers facing PFAS restrictions.
why: Turns the EU PFAS squeeze into market pull for a resource-light flow. PFC emissions per wafer fall ~50%+.

title: Substitute cryogenic argon aerosol jets for megasonic water rinses
idea: Expand chilled argon/nitrogen through a nozzle to form frozen micro-solids that knock 20 nm particles off the wafer by momentum transfer and then sublime, so no liquid ever touches the wafer.
why: Particle-removal passes use ~10-30 L UPW per wafer each; aerosol cleaning uses none (>50x cut) and avoids water-induced pattern collapse.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero indium and gallium (China-dominated). Build a 2T0C gain cell whose write transistor is amorphous Zn-Sn-O made by ALD below 300 C, Si-doped to suppress oxygen-vacancy leakage, with charge stored on the read transistor's gate.
why: Off-current near 1e-19 A/um stretches retention from 64 ms to minutes, removing most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh; uses earth-abundant Zn and little Sn instead of IGZO's critical metals.

title: Titanium and PEEK wetted paths for a fluoropolymer-free fab
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ti (22): once HF is gone from the fab, the main reason for PFA/PTFE plumbing disappears, so distribute UPW and oxidizing acids in electropolished titanium (passive TiO2 film) and use PEEK/high-purity polypropylene for reducing acids, solvents and slurries.
why: Fluoropolymers are the largest PFAS mass in a fab; removes that lifecycle liability with abundant Ti.

title: Mold compound becomes the substrate, deleting ABF and T-glass
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed LPDDR/DRAM dies face-down in a reconstituted epoxy-mold wafer and build the redistribution layers directly on it (fan-out wafer-level packaging). Each die nests inside its own package body, so neither organic build-up laminate (Ajinomoto ABF) nor low-CTE T-glass cloth (Nittobo) is needed.
why: Removes two near-single-supplier packaging chokepoints from memory modules and mobile DRAM, for ~20-30% lower package cost and lead time.

title: Purity in the code, not the crystal: solar-grade DRAM wafers
idea: Reverse where reliability lives: build DRAM on solar-grade silicon grown in ordinary quartz crucibles, accept that ~1% of cells have contamination-shortened retention, and protect each 4 KB page with an on-die LDPC code (~12% parity) that corrects a 1% raw BER.
why: Removes the 11N polysilicon and HPQ crucible chokepoints; wafer cost down ~20-30% for ~12% bit overhead.

title: Kovio's liquid-silicon ink revived as stacked polysilicon memory tiers on glass
idea: Kovio printed cyclopentasilane silicon ink for RFID and died because tiny printed tags could not beat wafer chips on cost per die. Memory is area-dominated: slot-die coat the ink over whole Gen-8 sheets, convert at ~400 C, flash-lamp crystallize to large-grain polysilicon, and stack poly-Si TFT memory tiers without vacuum CVD.
why: Silicon devices without Cz wafers or quartz crucibles; grams of silicon per m2 per tier; no PECVD/LPCVD vacuum energy; ~100 cm2/Vs poly-Si also makes on-glass periphery possible.

title: Croconic acid ferroelectric memory built only from carbon, hydrogen, oxygen
idea: Effect: croconic acid switches polarization (~20 uC/cm2, close to BaTiO3) by collective proton transfer along hydrogen-bonded chains at room temperature. Vacuum-sublime oriented films below 150 C as the last BEOL step and use them as the ferroelectric in FeFET or 1T-1C working memory.
why: Replaces Hf/Zr ferroelectrics and fluorinated PVDF (PFAS); a low coercive field allows sub-1 V writes; supply risk is zero because the element set is C, H and O.

title: Spacer cascade turns solar-grade screen printing into nanoscale lines
idea: Ideal: nanolines from the cheapest printing tool on Earth. Closest: screen- or gravure-print 10-20 um mandrel lines on panels or wafers, then run eight successive conformal-deposition/etch-back spacer cycles (each doubling line count, 2^8 = 256x) to reach ~50-80 nm-pitch gratings using only blanket depositions and etches.
why: 100x: swaps EUV/ArF capex for blanket steps costing ~$0.1-0.5/m2 each, cutting array patterning for panel memory >100x. Trades CD variation accumulated over cycles and supports only regular gratings.

title: Sand-battery thermal storage time-shifts fab furnaces to cheap solar
idea: Ideal: a fab powered by free sunshine. Closest: charge a resistively heated sand/firebrick thermal store (600-1000 C) with midday solar surplus, use it to preheat furnace, epi and abatement gases and drive absorption chillers overnight, and schedule flexible batch steps (diffusion, anneal, reclaim) into low-price hours.
why: Thermal loads are ~30-40% of fab energy; time-shifting can cut energy cost 20-30% and peak grid capacity, easing U.S. fab siting.

title: Cold-trap recovery of unreacted ALD metal precursors
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: put fore-line cryotraps and a valve synchronized to the precursor pulses on ALD chambers. The ~90-95% of metal-organic precursor (TEMAZr, TEMAHf, TDMAT, Ru/Co organometallics) that normally burns in abatement is condensed into returnable canisters for the supplier to redistill.
why: Cuts Hf, Zr, Ru and Co precursor demand per wafer ~3-10x. The ZAZ/HZO capacitor stack is among the highest-cycle-count ALD steps in DRAM.

title: Nuclear SMR co-located fab: one reactor powers, chills, purifies
idea: Combine an SMR's electricity, its steam and its low-grade heat into the fab's three biggest utilities: power for tools, steam-driven absorption chillers for process cooling, and waste heat for thermal desalination of UPW feedwater from brackish sources.
why: Cuts utility energy cost and carbon ~30% for a ~300 MW fab and decouples siting from fresh water and grid congestion, raising U.S. manufacturability.

title: Fab waste heat drives membrane distillation for zero liquid discharge
idea: Magnify water reuse to ~98%: route 40-60 C process-cooling return water through membrane-distillation stacks that purify spent rinse and scrubber water back to UPW feed, and crystallize the brine on site.
why: A DRAM fab draws ~10-20 million litres a day. Turning waste heat into water lets fabs site in dry US regions.

title: Space-station water recovery loop for zero-discharge DRAM fabs
idea: The ISS recovers ~98% of its water with vapor-compression distillation plus catalytic oxidation. Build fab ultrapure-water systems as zero-liquid-discharge loops: segregate rinse streams by contaminant, drive membrane distillation with 30-40 C fab waste heat, recover dilute HF and NH4OH, and return >90% of water to UPW.
why: A DRAM fab uses ~10 million gallons/day; >90% reuse unlocks siting in water-stressed Arizona, Texas and Idaho and removes water permits as a chokepoint for U.S. capacity.

title: Wastewater to ultrapure water with fab waste heat
idea: Inverts 'UPW starts from fresh water': feed the UPW plant from municipal treated wastewater, use the fab's 30-40 C chiller reject heat to drive membrane distillation ahead of RO/EDI polishing, and send reject brine to industrial users.
why: Eliminates freshwater withdrawal (a DRAM fab uses millions of gallons per day), opening drought-prone US sites and turning waste heat into a resource.

title: Distillery heat-recovery stills turn fab waste heat into UPW
idea: Whisky distilleries and desalination plants cascade heat through multi-effect stills; route the fab's 30-45 C process-cooling heat into membrane distillation modules that turn reject brine and rinse wastewater back into ultrapure-water feed, approaching zero liquid discharge.
why: A large DRAM fab draws ~20-40 million liters per day; recovering 70-90% of rinse water with free low-grade heat cuts withdrawals at drought-prone sites and RO energy.

title: Cryogenic hydrogen-fluoride etch opens mold holes without fluorocarbon gases
idea: Temperature/time shift: at -60 to -100 C, HF with water-vapor assist condenses as a self-limiting sidewall passivation layer. SiO2/SiN capacitor molds then etch fast without C4F6/C4F8 polymer passivation. The approach is shown for 3D NAND channel holes and would be ported to 60-115:1 DRAM capacitor molds.
why: Removes PFAS-class fluorocarbons from the highest-AR etch, with ~80% lower GWP and ~2x etch rate, helping reach AR ~115.

title: Strategic DRAM reserve banks wafers during gluts for shortages
idea: Time shift across the 3-4 year memory cycle: in glut years such as 2023, a government or consortium buys finished DRAM wafers and known-good dies from existing fabs near cost. They sit in nitrogen-purged dry cabinets (dies are stable for a decade) and are released to existing packaging lines in shortages like 2026.
why: Adds supply without any fab and keeps existing fabs at full load in downturns. A 5% annual-output buffer would have damped much of the 4x 2026 price spike.

title: Virtual metrology retires most monitor and dummy wafers
idea: Time shift from per-shift qualification to continuous checks: replace physical monitor wafers with models that fuse chamber RF, optical-emission and pressure traces with on-product scatterometry sites. Tools in existing trailing fabs are then qualified on product wafers.
why: Monitor and dummy wafers are 5-15% of wafer consumption. Cutting them ~70% frees CZ silicon, crucible demand and tool hours.

title: CVD silicon-carbide tubes and boats replace high-purity quartz furnaceware
idea: Time-shift consumable life: quartz tubes, boats and liners in existing furnaces devitrify and are swapped every few months. Drop-in CVD-SiC parts made from abundant Si and C (methyltrichlorosilane) last 5-10x longer and tolerate higher temperature.
why: Removes Spruce Pine high-purity quartz from furnace consumables in existing trailing fabs and cuts downtime.

title: Follow-the-sun memory lending across hemisphere datacenters
idea: Day-night time shift at planetary scale: memory-heavy batch jobs (checkpoint merges, analytics, embedding builds) migrate each evening to whichever region's daytime interactive load has fallen. The fleet then provisions DRAM for the planetary average rather than each site's peak.
why: Cuts installed DRAM an estimated 10-20% for the same work, with no new fab and no new wafers.

title: Chemical autarky: make fab chemistries on site from air, water and salt
idea: Inverts 'chemicals are purchased from concentrated suppliers': on-site electrolyzers make H2, O2 and ozone from water, chlor-alkali cells make HCl and Cl2 from salt, H2O2 comes from electrochemical oxygen reduction and NH3 from a small Haber-Bosch unit, all distilled to electronic grade at point of use.
why: Removes multi-week logistics and single-country dependencies for the highest-volume wet and gas chemicals; strengthens US manufacturability and resilience.

title: Chlorinated carborane photoacids replace perfluorinated sulfonates in DRAM resists
idea: A photoacid only needs a weakly coordinating conjugate base; the icosahedral carborane anion CB11H6Cl6- spreads its charge over 12 cage atoms, giving acid strength beyond triflic acid with zero C-F bonds. Pair it with triphenylsulfonium cations; the bulky cage also shortens acid diffusion for lower line-edge roughness.
why: Removes PFAS photoacid generators facing EU/US restriction from every ArF/EUV resist; boron is US-mined.

title: Microsecond flash anneal crystallizes strontium titanate on bare TiN
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rushing through the harmful window): deposit amorphous SrTiO3 by ALD on TiN and crystallize it with a ~1 ms flash-lamp pulse. The film reaches perovskite crystallization temperature before the TiN has time to oxidize into a low-k TiOx interlayer, which removes the Ru electrode that SrTiO3 capacitors historically needed.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k ~100-150 vs ~40 for ZAZ allows ~2x Cs or a pillar aspect ratio cut from ~70:1 to ~35:1, with no Hf or Ru (Sr, Ti and O are abundant).

title: On-die microheaters anneal away trap damage: heat to heal
idea: Magnify temperature briefly to minify aging: polysilicon heaters under each bank pulse to ~250 C for seconds during maintenance windows, annealing BTI traps and trap-assisted leakage paths so lower-margin, cheaper materials survive 10 years at 125 C.
why: Recovers drift in the retention tail and threshold voltage, which allows thinner dielectrics and abundant materials instead of over-engineered stacks.

title: Printed-electronics aqueous cluster inks replace organometallic ALD precursors
idea: Roll-to-roll printed-electronics makers spin aqueous inorganic clusters (Al13 hydroxo clusters, zirconium oxo-nitrate clusters) that densify into dense oxide films at ~300 C. Spin-coat AlOx/ZrOx dielectrics from water-based inks in a university fab and compare leakage, k and step coverage with ALD.
why: Removes costly, supply-concentrated organometallic precursors and vacuum tools from some dielectric layers; material use ~90% versus ~10-30% for ALD.

title: IBM-style memory leasing: makers own bits, reclaim and redeploy
idea: Revive IBM's 1950s practice of leasing core memory instead of selling it: DRAM makers lease modules by the GB-month, keep ownership, and are paid to reclaim, retest and redeploy them into second-life tiers.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: aligns incentives to stretch module life from ~5 to ~10 years, effectively raising supply; no EUV; claims 10-20% more bit-years per wafer.

title: Drop-tower silicon spheres skip crucibles, ingots and wire saws
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: melt granular polysilicon droplets in a drop tube so they solidify without a crucible into 1-2 mm single-crystal spheres (the Ball Semiconductor route). Pattern small memory chiplets on each sphere with conformal maskless lithography, and pack the spheres into 3D memory clusters.
why: Removes HPQ crucibles, ingot pulling and kerf loss (~40% of silicon) for small-die memory, for up to ~50% lower cost per wafer-equivalent if curved-surface lithography is solved.

title: Grow the holes: anodized alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: Inverts 'deep capacitor holes must be plasma-etched': deposit thick aluminum over the array and anodize it; self-ordered hexagonal pores with aspect ratios above 100:1 (pitch set by anodization voltage, registration seeded by a shallow imprint) become the capacitor mold, lined with electrode and dielectric by ALD.
why: Removes the hardest high-AR fluorocarbon etch (C4F6/C4F8, fluorspar and PFAS supply chain) and its hardmask stack; room-temperature aqueous electrochemistry reaches the AR~115 needed for more charge.

title: Strategic Petroleum Reserve model for helium, crucibles and WF6
idea: Copy the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and the Defense Logistics Agency stockpile: a federally chartered Semiconductor Materials Reserve holds 6-12 months of helium (re-using the Cliffside storage formation), HPQ crucible blanks, WF6/tungsten powder and neon, releasing them at pre-set price triggers and selling to fabs at cost in a disruption.
why: Turns shocks like the March-2026 Qatar outage or Hurricane Helene's 2024 Spruce Pine shutdown into non-events for U.S. DRAM and caps input spikes that feed the 4x price rise.

title: Gasless sustained self-sputtering ignited by a hydrogen pulse
idea: Box [Cu bitline / Ti liner | n/a | n/a | n/a | Si | HiPIMS sustained self-sputtering]: strike the magnetron with a 10 us H2 pulse, then keep the plasma alive purely on ionized target metal at >1 kW/cm2 peak power, giving a fully ionized, directional metal flux with zero working gas.
why: Removes Ar from metal PVD while improving bottom coverage in 60:1 features through ion-directed deposition, and eliminates trapped-Ar voids in films.

title: Ozone-gas and UV dry stripping to cut ultrapure water
idea: Periodic-table walk, O (8): replace sulfuric-peroxide resist strips and organic cleans with UV-activated O3 gas and humidified-ozone single-wafer dry oxidation, keeping wet steps only for metal and particle removal.
why: Cuts DRAM-fab UPW use ~30-50% and acid consumption; fluorine-free.

title: Tungsten-free DRAM: ALD molybdenum wordlines plus Cu-Mn bitlines
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | buried-channel Si RCAT | voltage SA | planar 1T1C | CZ Si | thermal ALD + electroplating]: fill buried wordlines with liner-free ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2/H2 and replace W bitlines, contacts and periphery plugs with electroplated Cu wrapped in a self-forming MnSiOx barrier.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%): removes essentially all W from the flow; Mo comes largely from US/Chile copper by-product, and dropping the TiN liner cuts wordline resistance ~30% at 10 nm width.

title: Architectural anodizing grows capacitor templates without plasma etch
idea: Window-frame anodizing grows self-ordered hexagonal nanopores in aluminum. Deposit an aluminum mold layer over the array, nano-indent pore seeds aligned to the storage-node landing pads, and anodize to grow straight pores of 1000:1 aspect ratio at ~40 nm pitch, then line them with ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN; nothing changes at the DDR/HBM pins.
why: Replaces the hardest high-aspect-ratio plasma etch (fluorocarbon gas, helium chuck cooling, carbon hard masks, hole patterning) with a bench-top electrochemical step; AR >100 at near-zero tool capital for ~2x Cs.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling in electrostatic chucks replaces helium
idea: Periodic-table walk, H (1): feed H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 W/mK, above He's 0.15) at 5-20 Torr behind wafers in etch/CVD chucks; sccm flows stay below the flammability limit with N2-diluted exhaust, and supply comes from on-site electrolysis.
why: Removes one of the largest fab helium uses during the Qatar outage; H2 comes from water.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnet bits switched by Neel-order spin-orbit torque
idea: Effect: the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn has a large anomalous Hall effect and tunnel magnetoresistance despite near-zero net moment. Switch its octupole order with current pulses and read it through Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn junctions, which removes IrMn pinning, Ru spacers and Pt torque layers.
why: Removes Ir, Ru and Pt (ultra-scarce PGMs) from magnetic memory; zero stray field allows denser packing, and ps-scale dynamics are possible; Mn and Sn are mined on several continents.

title: Stoichiometric-dose micro-gap ALD cuts zirconium and hafnium precursor tenfold
idea: A monolayer needs ~5e14 molecules/cm2, about 0.6 umol per 300 mm wafer per cycle, yet tools flow 20-50x that. Use a 0.2 mm-gap showerhead with stop-flow dose-and-hold exposure sized to the AR-squared Knudsen requirement of capacitor holes, so precursor dwells until consumed instead of streaming to the pump.
why: Precursor utilization rises from ~2-5% to ~30-40%: ~10x less Zr/Hf/Ti organometallic and abatement load per wafer.

title: Self-silicided titanium bitlines with column erasure coding
idea: Replace tungsten bitlines with TiSi2 formed in place from the bitline polysilicon (the conductor made from the material already there), accept the ~1% open/high-resistance columns from narrow-line agglomeration, and treat them as column erasures in the page code.
why: Removes W and WF6 from the bitline using abundant Ti; erasure decoding costs far less parity than random errors.

title: Catalyst-assisted wet etching digs 100:1 capacitor holes without fluorocarbon plasma
idea: Silicon dissolves only beneath a noble-metal catalyst in HF/H2O2 (metal-assisted chemical etching), so holes sink straight down at room temperature with no ion angular spread limiting depth. Pattern a catalyst mesh at storage-node pitch, sink 100:1 holes into silicon to revive trench-capacitor DRAM, then strip the catalyst in iodide etch.
why: Replaces the C4F6/C4F8 high-aspect-ratio plasma etch (PFAS-class gases, $10M+ tools, high energy) with a wet bench and pushes Cs past the 60-75:1 wall.

title: Hydrogen-free back end with titanium getters stabilizes oxide cells
idea: Minify the hydrogen inventory: deposit every dielectric above oxide-semiconductor transistors by ozone-ALD or PVD (no silane or NH3 PECVD), and wrap each array in a Ti/TiN getter cage so mobile hydrogen cannot reach channels during 10 years at 125 C.
why: Hydrogen drift is the main oxide-transistor failure at high temperature. Fixing it lets abundant-element oxide channels replace capacitors and most refresh.

title: Bubble memory reborn in manganese nitride with on-chip rotating fields
idea: Revive Bobeck's 1970s bubble memory without Gd/Ga garnet substrates: sputter perpendicular ferrimagnetic Mn4N on silicon, pattern permalloy asymmetric-disk propagation tracks, and drive every bubble with a 100 MHz rotating in-plane field from quadrature on-chip striplines. One global drive replaces per-cell transistors, and each minor loop needs just one magnetoresistive detector.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and scarce inputs: no gadolinium/gallium (China-dominated), no Hf or W, nonvolatile; a cheap nonvolatile spill tier for cold pages cuts DRAM per server; claims 3-5x lower cost per bit than DRAM.

title: Sealed nano-vacuum field-emission switches replace gate-oxide access transistors
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission. Mo nanotips face TiN anodes across a ~5 nm vacuum gap sealed by PECVD SiO2 at 350 C, forming the cell access device. Off-current falls exponentially with no thermionic subthreshold tail and no gate dielectric; field-enhanced tips switch on at ~2-3 V.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) and dependence on Hf high-k and single-crystal silicon; all steps are below 400 C.

title: Contamination-tolerant oxide memory built in warehouse-grade cleanrooms
idea: Ideal: memory that can be built in a garage. Closest: pick cell materials (wide-gap oxide channels, Al2O3, Mo) whose leakage is insensitive to Fe/Cu/Na at 10-100x semiconductor limits, and run them in ISO-6 sealed-minienvironment 'warehouse fabs' with display/solar-grade chemicals and gases costing ~5-10x less than ppt-grade.
why: 100x path: cleanroom, UPW and ultra-pure chemicals are ~30-40% of fab capex/opex; removing them, stacked on cheap-substrate tiers, cuts the cost stack toward 100x per GB and speeds U.S. buildout. Trades yield-learning risk and leakage margin.

title: PFAS-free DNQ-novolac resist revival for periphery layers
idea: Revive 1980s diazonaphthoquinone-novolac i-line resists, which contain no fluorinated photoacid generators, for every periphery and non-critical layer (about half the die), paired with second-hand i-line steppers.
why: PFAS phase-outs threaten chemically amplified resists, while DNQ is PFAS-free and cheap; no EUV; claims 50-60% of resist volume becomes PFAS-free at no cost penalty.

title: Acoustic and infrared watch lets crucibles survive extra pulls
idea: Within $1M/24 months: retrofit crystal pullers with acoustic-emission sensors and IR wall imaging that detect bubble growth and cristobalite spalling in the quartz crucible, so operators safely add one more recharge pull per crucible instead of retiring it on a fixed schedule.
why: One extra pull per crucible means ~20-50% fewer crucibles per kg of ingot, directly stretching Spruce Pine supply.
